firestoreSetup.title: Firestore setup needed
firestoreSetup.intro: The post and page list pages need a couple of Firestore composite indexes to query efficiently. They have to be created manually — Firebase reserves index creation for project admins.

firestoreSetup.step1: Click the link for each missing index — Firebase Console opens with the index definition pre-filled.
firestoreSetup.step2: Click "Create" and wait 1–5 minutes for the index to build (status badge in the console).

firestoreSetup.buildHint: Indexes can take up to a few minutes to build after creation.
firestoreSetup.unexpectedHint: Check your network connection and Firestore rules. If you just created the indexes, wait a moment for them to finish building, then retry.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Please read and accept the terms below before using AgentCMS. They are written in plain language to be quick to read.

section1.title: 1. Free service
section1.body: AgentCMS is provided to you free of charge. The usual charges of the services you choose (hosting, storage, Firebase…) still apply, on the accounts you own.

section2.title: 2. Provided as-is, no warranty
section2.body: The CMS is provided as-is. We work to keep it stable and improve it over time, but we cannot guarantee it will be free of bugs, defects or interruptions. Use it with the same caution you would any tool you didn't write yourself: keep backups of important content.

section3.title: 3. Your content, your responsibility
section3.body: You are solely responsible for the content you publish through the CMS — text, images, videos, forms, code embeds, and any other media. You must comply with applicable law in your jurisdiction (and in the jurisdictions you target), copyright, image and personality rights, personal data protection rules, and any third-party terms (e.g. embedded fonts or videos). The AgentCMS authors are not responsible for content published by users of the CMS.

section4.title: 4. Your Firebase account, your security
section4.body: The CMS stores its data in places you own (a git repository, a SQLite file, a Firebase project, this browser). You are responsible for securing them: strong passwords and passphrases, private repositories or buckets where needed, Firestore security rules as documented, token rotation, and reviewing who has access. The AgentCMS authors cannot be held responsible for unauthorised access, data leaks, hacks or losses caused by misconfiguration or compromise of those accounts.

section5.title: 5. Limitation of liability
section5.body: The AgentCMS authors cannot be held responsible for any loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, or any direct or indirect damages arising from the use, misuse, or unavailability of the CMS. Where applicable law requires them to assume some liability for the CMS, that liability is limited to the amount actually paid for the CMS over the past 12 months — which is zero, since the CMS is free.

section6.title: 6. Your data stays yours
section6.body: Content you create with the CMS is stored where you chose (text, settings, media metadata) and on your own hosting (the published HTML, images, theme assets). The CMS itself does not transmit your content to any third-party service. Plugins or themes you choose to enable may have their own behaviour — review what they do before activating them.

section7.title: 7. Fair use
section7.body: Do not use the CMS for unlawful, fraudulent, or harmful activities, or in ways that breach the terms of the services you connect it to. These terms may be updated over time; significant changes are listed in the release notes.

errors.firebaseAuthGeneric: Could not sign in to Firebase.
errors.firebaseAuthInvalidCredential: Firebase rejected the email + password combination.
errors.firebaseAuthInvalidCredentialHint:
Modern Firebase projects ship with email-enumeration protection on, which returns the same error whether the password is wrong, the user doesn't exist, or the user signs in with a different provider. Things to check:
• Re-enter the password — copy/paste from a password manager to rule out typos. Minimum length is 6 characters.
• Open Firebase Console → Authentication → Users and confirm the email exists. Check the 'Providers' column: if it shows only Google (or another provider) and not 'Email/Password', set or reset the password from the user's row menu (⋮ → Reset password).
• Verify the email spelling matches exactly what's stored in Firebase.

errors.firebaseAuthInvalidEmail: The admin email is not a valid email address.

errors.firebaseOperationNotAllowed: Email/password sign-in is not enabled on this Firebase project. Open Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method and enable the Email/Password provider.
errors.firebaseUserDisabled: This Firebase user account is disabled. Re-enable it from Firebase Console → Authentication → Users.
errors.wrongAdminEmail: The Firebase account you signed in with does not match the admin email you typed. Try again.
errors.rulesNotPinnedTitle: Firestore rules don't recognize you as bootstrap admin yet.
errors.rulesNotPinnedHint: Open Firebase Console → Firestore → Rules and replace the value of `bootstrapAdminEmail()` with: {{email}} — then click Publish. The rules template in the README ships with a `you@example.com` placeholder that must be replaced with your real admin email. After publishing the updated rules, click Submit here again.
errors.firestoreRulesHint: Open Firebase Console → Firestore → Rules and make sure the bootstrap admin email is set to '{{email}}'. The README has a copy-pastable rules template.

sqliteFile.security: No user accounts: anyone who can open this admin can edit the content — protect the admin folder at your hosting level. The database file is served like any other file: keep it encrypted, or store it in a separate private location.
sqliteFile.intro: Where the database file is stored. It is read and saved by this admin through the same connectors as the hosting.
sqliteFile.pathHint: Created on first save if it doesn't exist yet. With a Git repository, every save is a commit — prefer a repository or branch that doesn't trigger a site build.
sqliteFile.dataNote: Nothing to configure here: the database will be stored on the hosting you choose in the next step.
sqliteFile.heading: SQLite database
sqliteFile.encryptHint: Recommended on a public hosting: the file is unreadable without the passphrase. Each new browser asks for it once.
sqliteFile.passphraseHint: Save it in your password manager now: without it, nobody can open the database — not even you.
sqliteFile.passphraseTooShort: The passphrase must be at least 12 characters long.
sqliteFile.existingEncrypted: An encrypted database already exists at this path: enter its passphrase.
sqliteFile.separate: Store the database in a separate private location
sqliteFile.separateHint: E.g. a private S3 / R2 bucket or a private Git repository: the database is then never served by the public site.
sqliteFile.gitBranchNote: The database is kept on the branch {{branch}} of this repository, which is never published: saving content doesn't rebuild the site.
